questions.stem: A student uses a light microscope with an eyepiece magnification of x10 and an objective lens of x40. What is the total magnification?
questions.explanation: Total magnification is calculated by multiplying the eyepiece magnification by the objective lens magnification: 10 x 40 = x400. A common mistake is to add the two values (which would give x50), but they must be multiplied.

questions.stem: An electron microscope can see ribosomes, but a light microscope cannot. What property of the electron microscope allows this?

options.text: Higher resolution, allowing it to distinguish smaller structures

questions.explanation: Resolution is the ability to distinguish between two close points as separate objects. Electron microscopes have much higher resolution than light microscopes because electrons have a shorter wavelength than light. This allows subcellular structures like ribosomes to be seen clearly. Magnification alone without resolution would just produce a larger blurry image.

questions.stem: A scientist wants to observe how a living white blood cell engulfs bacteria. Which microscope should they use?
questions.explanation: A light microscope is the only option because electron microscopes require specimens to be dead and placed in a vacuum. Since the scientist wants to observe a living process (phagocytosis), a light microscope must be used, even though it has lower resolution.

questions.stem: A student prepares a microscope slide but the image is blurry even at low magnification. Which step did they most likely miss?

options.text: Adding a stain to the specimen
Using the fine focus knob before the coarse focus
Ensuring the specimen is thin enough for light to pass through
Placing the slide on the stage upside down

questions.explanation: Light microscopes work by passing light through the specimen. If the specimen is too thick, light cannot pass through effectively, resulting in a blurry or dark image. Specimens must be cut very thinly (or squashed) so that light can transmit through them to create a clear image.

questions.stem: A TEM image shows the internal structure of a cell in great detail, while an SEM image shows the 3D surface of a pollen grain. A researcher wants to study the arrangement of cristae inside mitochondria. Which should they use?

options.text: Light microscope, because mitochondria are large enough to see
TEM, because it shows detailed internal structures at high resolution
Any microscope would work equally well

questions.explanation: A TEM (Transmission Electron Microscope) passes electrons through thin slices of the specimen, revealing detailed internal structures (ultrastructure). Cristae are the inner folds of mitochondria, which are internal features requiring a TEM. An SEM only shows surface details, and a light microscope lacks the resolution to see cristae.
